subjects.displayTitle: Influence and centrality of the Word of God
subjects.introduction: Before there was a world there was a Word, and Bahá’u’lláh teaches that all existence came into being through it: a dewdrop from the ocean of divine grace, called in turn the Water of Life and the Primal Light. To believe this is to see creation itself as a book that speaks, and to find in the revealed verses a proof that shines among all other proofs as the sun among the stars. The same Word is water for souls perished in the wilderness of ignorance, the master key that unlocks the doors of hearts, the only sword permitted in a Revelation that has set the sword aside. By its power a shepherd became the guide of nations and a fisherman the repository of wisdom, and that power waits in every verse for whoever brings a pure ear and the capacity to hear. From here the path leads into the proofs of the Manifestations of God, into the transformation the Word works in a single soul, and into daily reading of the Sacred Writings, where an ocean of meanings opens.

In what sense is creation itself a book? Why should one word, letter or point be enough to bring a world into being?

shortened: Praise be to the all-perceiving, the ever-abiding Lord Who, from a dewdrop out of the ocean of His grace, hath reared the firmament of existence, adorned it with the stars of knowledge, and admitted man into the lofty court of insight and understanding. This dewdrop, which is the Primal Word of God, is at times called the Water of Life, inasmuch as it quickeneth with the waters of knowledge them that have perished in the wilderness of ignorance. Again it is called the Primal Light, a light born of the Sun of divine knowledge, through whose effulgence the first stirrings of existence were made plain and manifest.

These readings ask what the Word of God is. Bahá’u’lláh writes that it can never be confounded with the words of His creatures and is the King of words, that it is higher than what the senses perceive and sanctified from any substance, and that among human utterances the Divine Word is as the sun. The one revelation is called in one station the Word, in another the Will and in another the Divine Purpose, and God has made all words a throne for His Word. The Báb teaches that God has placed no intermediary between Himself and His chosen ones except His Word, the mirror that reflects its Speaker. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá and reported talks explain the opening of the Gospel of John, In the beginning was the Word, and the sense in which Christ was the Word. How can the Word be both the speech of God and the reality of the Manifestation? What follows from refusing to compare it with any other speech?
shortened: Say:  The Word of God can never be confounded with the words of His creatures.  It is, in truth, the King of words, even as He is Himself the sovereign Lord of all, and His Cause transcendeth all that was and all that shall be.

Why do the readings so often choose the humble as their examples?

These readings measure the power of the Word in the world. Bahá’u’lláh calls the Word the master key for the whole world, whose potency unlocks the doors of the hearts of men, and says that no might or power equals its penetrating influence. He proclaims that the law of the sword has been abolished and the law of utterance revealed, that victory in this Revelation has been confined to utterance, and that the cities of hearts must be conquered by the sword of utterance. Moses struck down the swords of the world with one staff, and the Ancient King has vanquished idle fancies with one Pen, which has not ceased despite every tribulation. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá compares the opposition of the clergy to a frail mosquito and the Word to a tempestuous wind, and says the only sword of the believers must be the Word of God. Why should utterance replace the sword? What does a conquest of hearts require of those who carry the Word?
shortened: O friend of mine!  The Word of God is the king of words and its pervasive influence is incalculable.  It hath ever dominated and will continue to dominate the realm of being.  The Great Being saith:  The Word is the master key for the whole world, inasmuch as through its potency the doors of the hearts of men, which in reality are the doors of heaven, are unlocked.

order.why: These readings ask what the Word does among the peoples. Reported talks warn that peace documents will remain dead letters without it and that universal peace cannot be established by thought alone, and point to fellowship across race in America and among pilgrims of every background. What can the Word achieve that agreements, science and good intentions cannot? Where do the readings place the believers in this work?

These principles are finite and limited, but the Word of God comprehendeth all true principles, and deriveth moreover its enforcing power from the breaths of the Holy Spirit. Hence It encompasseth and overshadoweth each and all.

These readings consider the hearer. The same verses, the Báb writes, are a light to those who believe and a fire to those who turn away, and Bahá’u’lláh says the believers quaff from them the wine of everlasting life while the ungodly drink a scalding draught. The penetrating influence of the Word depends upon the sanctification of the heart and emanates from its sincerity; the Pen flows only with what the people are capable of bearing, and today the station of the Word is concealed because of the people’s lack of capacity. Names and words have become veils. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá observes that oil ignites at once on touching fire while black stone does not, and reported talks apply Christ’s parable of the seed. Whoever gives ear to the Call is among the most distinguished souls, though a carrier of ashes. What makes a heart able to hear? Why do the same words heal one soul and harden another?
shortened: Yet the radiance of the visible sun is perceived by the outward eye, whereas the radiance of the Sun of the Word is perceived by the inward eye. By Him in Whose hand is my soul: should, for one moment, the inner aid and power of the Word of God be cut off from the world and its people, all would become nonexistent and be brought to naught. And if any soul look with the eye of God, he shall behold its light and splendour in all things; and likewise, if he turn, with a pure ear by God's leave, he shall hearken, at every hour, unto the primal divine Call.
Leprosy may be interpreted as any veil that interveneth between man and the recognition of the Lord, his God.
We bear witness that through the power of the Word of God every leper was cleansed, every sickness was healed, every human infirmity was banished.

These readings open the oceans of meaning. Bahá’u’lláh bids the people immerse themselves in the ocean of His words to discover the pearls of wisdom hidden in its depths, and declares that He has not revealed a mere code of laws but unsealed the choice Wine. In each letter an ocean of meanings lies concealed, and within speech lies the treasury of silence. The readings show the Pen interpreting the wine of the Crimson Book as the Most Great Word, explain which divine words may be interpreted, and warn against interpreting God’s words according to one’s desires, against entrusting one’s insight wholly to others and against grasping the letters while casting away the meanings. A verse recited for centuries may never have been pondered, and a reported talk explains why heavenly teachings are expressed in parables. How can a reader go beneath the outward meaning without imposing a personal one?
shortened: Think not that We have revealed unto you a mere code of laws. Nay, rather, We have unsealed the choice Wine with the fingers of might and power. To this beareth witness that which the Pen of Revelation hath revealed. Meditate upon this, O men of insight!
Immerse yourselves in the ocean of My words, that ye may unravel its secrets, and discover all the pearls of wisdom that lie hid in its depths.
